4.17.4.en: v When you are occupied with some sin, be an accuser of yourself (Prov 18:17), and do not wait for others to bring the accusation. Thus you become like a righteous man who accuses himself in his first speech in court, or like Job, whom the crowd of the people in the city did not hinder from declaring his crime before all [21].

4.17.5.en: v Confess to the Lord with the lute, with a harp of ten strings sing to Him" (Ps 33:3)

4.17.6.en: We begin by confessing to the Lord with a harp, that is, by ordering our bodily conduct, for if we have sinned with our body, when we presented our members as an instrument for sin to do evil, our body ought to confess the fault by using the same instrument to wipe out sin (Rom 6:19)

4.17.7.en: Have you insulted anyone? Speak well of him!

4.17.8.en: Have you abused your authority? Return what you took!

4.17.9.en: Have you satisfied the desire of your belly? Fast!

4.17.10.en: Have you been proud? Be humble!

4.17.11.en: Have you refused to take for the sake of your dignity? Ask!

4.17.12.en: Have you killed? Bear the sufferings of martyrdom or what is equivalent to them.

4.17.13.en: Break your body by open confession. After this open confession, you deserve to praise the Lord with a harp of ten strings.

4.17.14.en: You must first treat the sins of your body so that you may walk in harmony and concord toward perfection through the word of God, and rise until you behold spiritual goods. For the soul that seeks heavenly goods is called a harp, and it has the shape of the harp, since the notes come from its upper part, and the works of the body confess to God from below, but the mysteries that are revealed to knowledge come from above, and in the soul is the echo of the Spirit.

4.17.15.en: He who works by all the commandments forms from them a beautiful symphony. He sings to God on a harp of ten strings, referring to the Ten Commandments written in the Law [22].

4.18.s.en: What is our attitude toward him whom his conscience does not condemn (so he does not confess his sins)?

4.18.0.en: v Question: What if (the person) says: "My conscience does not condemn me"?

4.18.1.en: Answer: The same thing also happens with bodily diseases. For there are many diseases that those afflicted with them do not perceive. Yet they trust the physician's diagnosis more than their own personal lack of feeling of the disease. So also with the diseases of the soul, that is, sins. If someone is unaware of his sin, so he does not condemn himself, yet he must trust those who can see his condition more clearly. This is shown by the holy Apostles, who, despite their conviction of their sincere inclination toward the Lord, yet when they heard: "One of you shall betray me" (Mt 26:21), preferred to trust the word of the Lord, and yielded to His saying, saying: "Lord, is it I?" (Mt 26:22).

4.18.2.en: As for St. Peter, he teaches us more clearly, for although in the zeal of his humility he refused the service of his Master and God and Teacher (to wash his feet), when he heard the words of the Lord: "If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me" (Jn 13:8), he was convinced of the truth as it came in the words, and said: "Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head" (Jn 13:9) [23].

4.18.3.en: St. Basil the Great Do not subject yourself [24] to a foolish man, and do not show partiality to the face of a ruler [27].

4.18.4.en: It is good that a man walk in the spirit of humility, but for the sake of the believer's concern for his own salvation and the salvation of his brothers he must not hand over the leadership of his life into the hand of a fool, who corrupts his mission and brings him into troubles; and it also stirs in the fool the spirit of pride and his failure to review his follies.

4.18.5.en: The spirit of humility does not mean cringing before any leader whatever his role at the expense of the needy and the oppressed.

4.19.0.en: Strive for the truth unto death, and the Lord God will fight for you [28].

4.19.1.en: The wise man urges us to (spiritual) striving for the truth unto death [28]. And he who lays down his life for the truth, the Lord fights on his behalf. So he is not ashamed to witness to his faith, whatever the cost.

4.19.2.en: v "Strive for the truth unto death" (Sir 4:28). From the very same spiritual treasures are made the crowns of the martyrs for the truth, to be set upon their heads, and that with everyone who takes part in the spiritual battles, so (the believer) treads upon those who kindle conflicts and those known as the rulers of the world and the authorities over the darkness of this age and the spiritual hosts of wickedness (Eph 6:12; Sir 4:28; Song 3:10) [25].

4.19.3.en: St. Didymus the Blind v He who takes part in the Olympic games is crowned not by his victory over one or two or three players, but after his victory over all of them. So he who wishes God to crown him must learn chastity, not only with respect to bodily passions, but also to overcome in the temptation of the love of money and the desire to cling to what is not his, and envy and the love of pleasures and vainglory and being accused of base things and when mortal dangers befall him, and so on [26].

4.19.4.en: v Let us strive in the good life and the God-loving life, not for the praise of men, but for the salvation of our souls. For death stands before our eyes every day, and because everything human is unstable [27].

4.19.5.en: St. Anthony the Great St. Augustine distinguishes between three kinds of witnesses to the Lord Christ.

4.19.7.en: The first class includes him who believes in Christ and scarcely whispers His name.

4.19.8.en: And the next class is he who believes in Christ and confesses openly.

4.19.9.en: And the third is he who believes in Christ and confesses Him, and is ready to die for Christ.

4.19.10.en: The first is weak and his shame rests on his fear, the second bears courage on his face but not to the shedding of his blood, the third has all strength and lacks nothing he desires; he is truly as it is written: "Strive for the truth unto death" [28]

4.19.11.en: St. Augustine Origen sees in the ritual of the tabernacle of meeting or the temple the existence of two altars, one visible and the other invisible. The visible altar is the bronze altar on which the burnt offerings are offered, referring to our spiritual striving for the divine truth unto death. For if our Christ offered His body given up to the death of the cross, we are crucified with Him, and practice the mortification of the body through the burnt offering of pure love. As for the hidden altar, the high priest enters to it in the Holy of Holies, which refers to heaven and entry to the divine throne.

4.19.12.en: Thus Origen presents to us a symbolic interpretation of the burnt offering in his inner depths as a symbol of the mortification of the body through the fiery Holy Spirit of God, where he renounces everything for the sake of divine truth and love, bearing the cross like his Master with joy and delight; we quote from him the following:

4.19.13.en: v Each one of us also has himself as a whole burnt offering, and he himself kindles the altar of the whole burnt offering so that it may be consumed.

4.19.14.en: If I renounce all that I have (Lk 14:33), and take up my cross, and follow Christ (Mk 8:34), I offer a whole burnt offering on the altar of God. Or if I deliver my body even to martyrdom, I offer myself as a whole burnt offering on the altar of God.

4.19.15.en: If I love my brothers, and lay down my life for my brothers (1 Jn 3:16), if for righteousness and truth I strive unto death (Sir 4:28), I offer a whole burnt offering on the altar of God.

4.19.16.en: If I mortify my members from every lust of the flesh (Col 3:5), if the world has been crucified to me and I to the world (Gal 6:14), I offer a whole burnt offering on the altar of God, and I myself become a priest of the offering [28].

4.19.17.en: v You also have a calf that you must offer. This unruly calf is your body; if you wish to offer it to the Lord as an offering, keep it ascetic and pure, lead it to the door of the tabernacle of meeting, where you can hear the reading of the Holy Scriptures there.

4.19.18.en: Let your offering be a male... so that there may be in it nothing of pampering or lack of firmness.

4.19.19.en: Lay your hand upon the burnt offering that it may be acceptable to the Lord, and slay it before the Lord, meaning that you set limits of chastity and do not abandon the subduing of the body, but be like him who laid his hand upon his body when he said: "I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway" (1 Cor 9:27).

4.19.20.en: Slay it before the Lord and do not hesitate to mortify your members (Col 3:5)...

4.19.21.en: Let there be within you a priest and his sons, that is, the spirit that is in you and its senses, for through them there is understanding of the Lord and perception of divine knowledge. Then offer your body to the Lord in asceticism but with spiritual understanding, as the Apostle says: "a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service" (Rom 12:1)...

4.20.0.en: Some offer their bodies as a burnt offering but as though without a priest, that is, without fullness of knowledge... These are put to shame, for they seek human glory (in their asceticism), or are defiled by the desire of covetousness or by committing the fault of envy or malice, or are troubled by the agitation of hatred or the harshness of anger. These practice bodily asceticism but offer a burnt offering without a priest, that is, without understanding or perception, so they are counted among the five foolish virgins who were truly ascetic in body as virgins, but did not know how to put oil in their vessels, that is, the oil of love and peace with the rest of the virtues. Therefore they were driven out of the bridal chamber of the bridegroom (Mt 25)... But as for us, it is fitting for us, with the asceticism of the body, to be pure in spirit... so that we may be made worthy to be like Christ the sacrifice [29].

4.21.0.en: v The person who has not yet become spiritual but is carnal, is defeated by any (vice), even against his will. For his will is not yet strong and vigorous enough to decide within itself to be committed to striving unto death for the truth (Sir 4:28). This kind of will does not say: yes yes and no no (Mt 5:27). Thus it cannot do what it wills, but what it does not will... because Christ does not yet dwell in him (Rom 8:10) and his body has not become a temple of God (1 Cor 3:16; 6:19) [30].

4.22.0.en: v I offer a whole burnt offering on the altar of God if I put my members to death from every lust of the flesh; if the world has been crucified to me and I to the world (Gal 6:14). I offer a whole burnt offering on the altar of God, and I myself become a priest of my offering [31].

4.23.0.en: Origen v "I have seen an end of all perfection: but thy commandment is exceeding broad" (Ps 119:96). When he went into the sanctuary of God, he understood the last things (Ps 73:17). Now the whole end draws near to me in this place to help me to strive for the truth unto death (Sir 4:28), and to endure every evil for the sake of the chief true good. The end is by ascending into the kingdom of Christ, which has no end, there where there is neither death nor pain, but an honored life that is achieved by dying to this life and enduring sorrows and shame [32].

4.23.1.en: St. Augustine Do not be harsh in your tongue, nor slack and lazy in your works [29].

4.23.2.en: It is fitting for the believer not to be hasty in speech, but to examine matters with deliberation before he utters his opinion. On the other hand it is not permitted for him to be slow in work through negligence.

4.23.3.en: Do not be as a lion in your house, and do not be a mockery among your servants [30].

4.23.4.en: It is not fitting for the believer to practice violence in his house, for no one accepts to live in a black pit.

4.23.5.en: Do not stretch out your hand to receive, and close it when it should repay [31].

4.23.6.en: The hand must be stretched out to give, not to receive [31]. Let the believer know when to keep his hand stretched out and when to close it.

4.23.7.en: v Some share in the head (concerning the paschal lamb), and others in the breast, and others in the inwards, and others in the thigh, and others even in the feet, where there is not much meat. Each one shares according to his capacity. And we share in a part of the true Lamb in accordance with our ability to share in the word of God. For some of us share in the head, and if we wish, in a part of it, for example in the ears, so that, as they become possessed of ears, they can hear His words (cf. Mt 11:15; 13:9, 43).

4.23.8.en: And some taste the eyes, and they see clearly (cf. Ps 34:9; Heb 6:4-5), so that his foot does not strike against a stone (cf. Ps 91:12; Jer 13:16; Mt 4:6; Lk 4:11).

4.23.9.en: And those who taste the hands are the workers (cf. Jn 9:4), who no longer have slack hands (Heb 12:12), closed against giving (Sir 4:31), those who accept the correction of their course before the wrath of the Lord falls upon them (cf. Ps 2:11).

4.24.0.en: And others lean on the breast (Jn 25:13), and recognize through that food those who betrayed Christ (cf. Jn 13:21-26) [33].

4.25.s.en: Lead me as a son of Yours among my brothers!

4.25.0.en: v How sweet is Your commandment to me: to love my neighbor as myself.

4.25.1.en: And how great is the power of Your grace, for it leads me to do the commandment in a spirit of joy and exultation.

4.25.2.en: I walk by Your Holy Spirit as Your ambassador.

4.25.3.en: You made me a member of the family that includes all humanity.

4.25.4.en: I benefit from the experiences of former generations, and touch Your wonderful dealings with them.

4.25.5.en: And I do not withdraw from my brothers in the present generation, but with love I embrace all in a spirit of gladness, I feel my need of every man, with my commitment to work with everyone according to my abilities!

4.25.6.en: I look to the coming generations and ask:

4.25.7.en: What shall I do for my children and grandchildren who will come through the coming ages?

4.25.8.en: v As I meet the poor and needy man whom You count a brother to You, You who are the Creator of heaven and earth, I stretch out my hand to give of what You have given me.

4.25.9.en: I feel ashamed, because I offer You little of what You gave me.

4.25.10.en: All that is in my hand is from Your blessings and gifts.

4.25.11.en: v Grant me the sweet word with giving, by which I gladden all hearts.

4.25.12.en: The whole world needs You and Your sweetness and tenderness!

4.25.13.en: You are my precious treasure; the more I offer You to my brothers, the more You shine forth in my depths.

4.25.14.en: v Let me walk by Your Holy Spirit, so that I stretch out my hands to all, indeed open my heart especially to the suffering and needy and oppressed and to those who have no one to ask after them, and the enemy of good does not steal into me and drive me to partiality.

4.25.15.en: That I may be like You, for You have given me the spirit of sonship.

4.25.16.en: I have become in the eyes of the heavenly beings a son of the Most High.

4.25.17.en: So do not allow anyone to be embittered of soul because of me, for I desire that You establish Your Kingdom in the heart of every man.

4.25.18.en: Grant me the spirit of humility, that I may offer honor to whom honor is due without partiality.

4.25.19.en: v Lead me in the narrow way of wisdom, that I may carry Your cross with You, and experience the joy of Your resurrection.

4.25.20.en: I rise early to You continually, and cast myself into Your divine embrace.

4.25.21.en: I experience the earnest of heaven day by day, until I meet You on the clouds, and enjoy the procession of Your eternal wedding.

4.25.22.en: Your wisdom embraces me as a mother and a bride, pouring into me the spirit of holiness, so that I serve You, O Holy One.

4.25.23.en: I hold on to You that You may accompany me all the way, so that I do not turn to the right nor to the left.

4.25.24.en: Do not forsake me, for I cannot live without You.

4.25.25.en: Keep me from evil, and draw me to Your righteousness.

4.25.26.en: v Grant me, O Lord, a heart burning with love toward fallen souls.

4.25.27.en: I plant my foot firm by Your grace, so that I do not fall with the one thrown on the ground, that I may raise him by Your grace.

4.25.28.en: Often my soul longs to practice the training of holy silence, lest I stumble because of the tongue.

4.25.29.en: Grant me wisdom that my silence may be made holy by You, and my words holy also.

4.25.30.en: So I am silent at the right time, and do not hold back the holy word at its right time!

4.25.31.en: v Teach me to speak confessing my sins, so that my whole being becomes a harp singing to You the hymn of thanksgiving, O Forgiver of sins.

4.25.32.en: v Grant me not to be hasty in speech without thought, nor to be slack in work, in what fulfills Your plan in my serious life.
